To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can use linear multistep methods to solve a class of structured DAEs, without the need of the strict stability of second characteristic polynomial, which is usually required in existing literature.
we have developed a class of linear multisteps discretizations for a special class of DAEs.
for a class of DAEs, a linear multisteps discretization scheme with an appropriate reformulation may be used to achieve the same convergence rate and stability property as applied for ODEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two issues.

the numerical solution of the following DAEs: $F(t,y,\frac{dy}{dt})=0, \frac{dy}{d t} = f(t, y), y(t_0) = y_0,$ where $F: R \times R^n \times R^n\rightarrow R^n$ is a smooth function, $f:R \times R^n → R^n$ is continuous and $y_0 ∈ R^n$ is given.
a new discretization method for a class of strangeness-free DAEs and a new class of linear multisteps schemes with the same stability property and convergent order as applied to ODEs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the DAE class under investigation the new discretization methods are more efficient than the existing ones, and that the new methods can be applied to more general DAEs.

, when the underlying linear multstep method is implicit, the numerical solution obtained from the proposed discretization schemes is more stable than the solution obtained from the standard discretization schemes; when the underlying linear multistep method is implicit, there is no significant difference in the stability of the solution between the two discretization schemes.

for this class of structured strangenes free DAEs, it is possible to use linear multistep methods to achieve a stable and efficient discretization scheme without the requirement of strict stability for the second characteristic polynomial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new discretization method is more stable than the existing ones and the computational cost may also be reduced.
for a class of strangeness free DAs, the linear multistep methods are stable and can be applied to the DAEs directly without the need of reformulation.
for a class of strangeness free DAFs the strict stability of their second characteristic polynomial is not necessary for the zero stability of linear multisteps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a class structured DAEs, linear multistep methods can be used to solve the DAEs in the same way as applied to ODEs.
for some classes of semi linear DDAEs, explicit linear multistep methods may be used as underlying discretizations.
the stability requirement of the underlying linear multstep methods for DAEs can be relaxed, and the stability requirement of linear multisteps methods for ODEs can be applied to DAEs.
